title: Sunrise Health Renewal & Capacity Strategy - Check-in
topics: Capacity bump across EU and APAC
Private deployment vs Dedicated pool tradeoffs
action_items: Maya - Share updated pricing sheet with tiered burst rates by 2025-07-04
Luca - Run 95th perc latency benchmark for eu-west-1 private pilot and share traces by 2025-07-09
Priya - Provide list of 3 compliance questions for SOC2/KMS integration by 2025-07-06
Jason - Confirm internal procurement cadence and PO window (EOM vs net30) by 2025-07-08
next_steps: Send contract amendment draft for +30% capacity and 12-month extension
Schedule technical pilot run for EU private node (2-week window) - tentative start 2025-07-14
Luca to open an email thread with operations with perf spreadsheet and endpoint config
transcript_header:
Date: 2025-07-02 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Singh, Luca Romano (Redwood) - Dr. Elena Ruiz, Mark Thompson, Priya Iyer, Jason Cole (Sunrise Health)
summary: Check-in to align on renewal timing and capacity uplift for EU + APAC. Customer leaning toward a mixed approach: Dedicated reserved capacity for peak US traffic, Private (VPC) nodes for EU PHI-sensitive workloads, and short-term burst tiers for APAC. Action items agreed around pricing, a short performance pilot, and clarifying KMS / audit log expectations.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — we have 42 minutes on the calendar, quick check-in on renewal and the capacity plan.
[00:12] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Hi Maya, hi Luca, thanks. We want to make sure we don't have any surprises going into Q4, especially with EU PHI workloads and the new APAC region traffic.
[00:23] Maya: Totally, and congratulations on the product launch last month — saw the notes. Quick qual question, has your traffic baseline changed since our last call? You mentioned an uplift.
[00:34] Mark Thompson: Yeah baseline's up about 22% month-over-month, peak windows are spicy — late evenings EU and morning APAC. We're seeing a longer tail of requests which spikes KV cache misses.
[00:47] Luca: When you say KV cache misses, is that mostly on the session affinity routes or across the board?
[00:53] Priya: Mostly across the board, but more pronounced on the clinical NLP endpoints. We're also experimenting with quantized models which helped cost, but some latency regressions popped up.
[01:05] Maya: Right, so two levers: model quant and routing, and then capacity geometry. For renewal, you mentioned wanting a 12-month extension with a 30% uplift; is that still the ask?
[01:16] Dr. Elena: Yes, rough numbers. We'd like reserved capacity for core US traffic, private (VPC) nodes in eu-west for PHI, and then burst capacity for APAC during launches. Cost is a big factor.
[01:28] Jason: From procurement side we also need a cleaner data residency clause and KMS/HSM details. SOC 2 attestation is required too.
[01:36] Maya: Understood. We can include KMS integration notes and SOC 2 reports. Luca, maybe walk through the Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs?
[01:44] Luca: Sure. Dedicated (reserved pools) gives you predictable throughput and is the lowest per-token cost at steady-state. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you control over the data plane and key management — higher operational overhead, and latency depends on your peering. For EU PHI, private is common because of data sovereignty and audit log control.
[02:03] Mark: How much overhead are we looking at to run the private control plane vs Dedicated? Our ops team is... small.
[02:11] Luca: On our managed Private option, Redwood still runs the inference nodes but they sit in your VPC; setup typically takes 2-4 weeks for eu-west prep and certs. On-prem is heavier. Dedicated is simpler — we provision GPU pools in our cloud with reserved capacity, takes 3-7 days.
[02:27] Priya: For the private node, do you support customer KMS and HSM?
[02:31] Maya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS keys and can integrate with common HSM providers; there is an onboarding checklist. We'll share tech notes.
[02:40] Dr. Elena: And about latency — our SLO is 150ms 95th on the clinical endpoint. Can Redwood consistently deliver that from eu-west?
[02:50] Luca: We'll need to tune model variants and batch sizing. Also recommend prefix/KV caching. For eu-west private nodes, we've seen 95th in the 120-160ms range depending on model and sequence lengths. I'll run a focused benchmark to get you numbers for your payload distribution.
[03:10] Mark: Can you also test with our payload set? We have longer sequences (avg 900 tokens) for the report summarization.
[03:18] Luca: Absolutely — please share a sanitized sample and I'll run it.
[03:22] Jason: About pricing — if we lock 12 months and bump capacity 30%, can we get tiered burst credits for APAC launches?
[03:30] Maya: We can price a committed tier with a burst pool on top — typically burst is higher per-unit but we can include monthly burst credits as part of the amendment. I'll send a few pricing scenarios.
[03:41] Priya: Any concerns about model quantization impacting clinical accuracy? We can't have hallucination regressions.
[03:47] Luca: Good point. Our Optimize tool recommends quant profiles that balance perf and quality; we also recommend running regression evals against a labeled prompt set. We can help set up a small eval harness.
[03:58] Dr. Elena: What's the rollback story if a quantized model shows quality drift in prod?
[04:04] Luca: Canary rollouts + automatic fallback to a verified full-precision variant. Redwood's routing policies can route a small percent to the new variant and auto-fallback on regression thresholds.
[04:15] Maya: Let's talk timeline. You're retendering or just renewing?
[04:19] Dr. Elena: We're in renewal but also kicking procurement checklists — likely signing an amendment by late July, want pilot results before finalizing.
[04:28] Maya: OK makes sense. So next: we'll send price scenarios, Luca will run perf tests with your sample, and we'll draft the amendment. Any red flags?
[04:38] Mark: One more: audit log retention. We need 7 years for certain audit trails for a subset of metadata, though not all payload. Do you support customizable audit retention?
[04:48] Luca: We can set configurable retention on logs and can filter PII out of longer-term archives. Need to consult security on policy, but technically doable.
[04:57] Jason: Also, SSO — we need SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[05:02] Maya: Redwood supports SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, yes. We'll include an SSO setup guide.
[05:09] Dr. Elena: For the EU private node, can you guarantee data doesn't leave the eu-west cluster?
[05:15] Luca: Yes, for private nodes we pin the inference nodes to the region; control plane traffic can be minimal and we can discuss routing to avoid cross-region egress.
[05:25] Priya: On the pilot, we want to validate both latency SLO and KMS key rotation behavior.
[05:31] Luca: Noted. I'll include key rotation tests and show logs for rotation events.
[05:36] Maya: Any competitive things we should be aware of?
[05:39] Dr. Elena: BigCloud AI offered lower burst pricing but no private VPC option; NimbusServe pushed a full on-prem hardware option but at much higher ops cost. So Redwood's mixed approach looks attractive.
[05:53] Maya: Great. I'll put together three pricing scenarios: reserved-heavy, mixed private+Dedicatd, and burst-focused.
[06:00] Mark: Dedicatd?
[06:02] Maya: (laughing) Sorry, Dedicated — speech to text hiccup.
[06:07] Dr. Elena: Any questions from your side?
[06:09] Priya: Implementation detail — do you surface token-level cost by route? We need to map cost back to product features.
[06:16] Luca: Yes, Console provides token-level cost and per-route dashboards, you can tag endpoints. We can demo a cost breakdown in the pilot readout.
[06:24] Jason: Procurement asks if you can accept a master service agreement plus an amendment?
[06:29] Maya: Yes, MSS + amendment is typical. We'll share the amendment template.
[06:33] Dr. Elena: OK, to recap: pricing scenarios, perf run with our sample on eu-west private node, SOC2/KMS docs, SSO guide, and contract draft.
[06:43] Maya: Correct. Action owners we put in the notes. Thank you all, we'll follow up in email and schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of 2025-07-14.
[06:53] Dr. Elena: Thanks everyone. Bye.
[06:56] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., Dedicatd) and speaker overlap at 06:00-06:10 where crosstalk occurred.
file_notes: Pilot focuses: eu-west private node perf + KMS rotation checks. Customer wants 12-month extension +30% capacity with tiered burst credits for APAC. Procurement needs SOC2 and PO cadence.
